title: OmniShow: Unifying Multimodal Conditions for Human-Object Interaction Video Generation
claim: One unified model handles many combinations of input conditions and extends to new applications, all with high-quality outputs.
layout: 2 stacked sections, grid of colored task cards, central logo divider
description: The figure has two sections split by a central OmniShow logo. Section (a), Unified Tasks, is a 2x2 grid of pastel cards (yellow, blue, green, peach). Each card shows input icons and reference images on the left: text, image, pose skeleton and audio waveform. An arrow leads to a row of generated video frames of a person holding a product. Captions give the task names R2V, RP2V, RA2V and RAP2V, with the conditions increasing from text and images up to audio and pose. Section (b), Broader Applications, has three cards: audio-driven avatars (a robot with a waveform), video remixing (pose, object and human combined) and object swapping (original frames above, swapped-product frames below). The eye lands first on the bright photographic frames and the logo in the middle.
caption: Overview of OmniShow. Our model unifies text, reference image, audio, and pose conditions to synthesize high-quality videos. (a) Unified Tasks: OmniShow exhibits exceptional flexibility across diverse conditioning settings, from R2V, RA2V, RP2V to the most challenging RAP2V, consistently delivering industry-grade visual quality and precise multimodal alignment. (b) Broader Applications: OmniShow unlocks creative potential such as audio-driven avatars, object swapping, and video remixing, demonstrating robust compositional control and extensible capabilities. Please visit our project page for more immersive and diverse video demonstrations.
abstract: In this work, we study Human-Object Interaction Video Generation (HOIVG), which aims to synthesize high-quality human-object interaction videos conditioned on text, reference images, audio, and pose. This task holds significant practical value for automating content creation in real-world applications, such as e-commerce demonstrations, short video production, and interactive entertainment. However, existing approaches fail to accommodate all these requisite conditions. We present OmniShow, an end-to-end framework tailored for this practical yet challenging task, capable of harmonizing multimodal conditions and delivering industry-grade performance. To overcome the trade-off between controllability and quality, we introduce Unified Channel-wise Conditioning for efficient image and pose injection, and Gated Local-Context Attention to ensure precise audio-visual synchronization. To effectively address data scarcity, we develop a Decoupled-Then-Joint Training strategy that leverages a multi-stage training process with model merging to efficiently harness heterogeneous sub-task datasets. Furthermore, to fill the evaluation gap in this field, we establish HOIVG-Bench, a dedicated and comprehensive benchmark for HOIVG. Extensive experiments demonstrate that OmniShow achieves overall state-of-the-art performance across various multimodal conditioning settings, setting a solid standard for the emerging HOIVG task.
